Cauchy perimeter formula and standard positive finite Hankel moment reconstruction
correctness.rationale: For an arbitrary compact convex planar W with perimeter P and finitely many distinct strictly interior centers, r<min(boundary distance,half minimum center separation) ensures separate holes. A generic invariant line meeting W intersects the convex window in one segment; each transversal disk hit removes one interval, so C_r-1=sum I_i. Normalization integral_0^pi width_W(theta)dtheta=P. Joint offset overlap for pair separation d is (2r-d|cos theta|)_+ and angular integral equals 2d F(2r/d), F(s)=s asin(s)+sqrt(1-s²)-1. Thus G=E binom(C_r-1,2)=(2/P)sum d F(2r/d), unaffected by triple hits. F'(s)=asin s and positive c_k=binom(2k-2,k-1)/[4^(k-1)(2k-1)(2k)] yield μ_j=sum d^(-2j-1) from even Taylor coefficients. The first 2M μ_j for M=binom(n,2) determine the positive atomic measure at t=d^-2, with weights multiplicity*d^-1 via rank of Hankel matrix, annihilating polynomial and Vandermonde; repeated distances are recovered. The actual package checker performs exact-rational repeated-distance recovery, angular quadrature and conditional-line simulation, read here but not used as infinite proof.

Jiao–Stillinger–Torquato homometric configurations show why distance multiset is the correct limited target
value.rationale: Recovery of an unordered Euclidean distance spectrum from one scalar line-section topology observable as a radius varies is an independently motivated geometric inverse problem. Positive Hankel inversion handles repeated distances constructively, and the containing convex window influences the observation only through its perimeter. The paper carefully does not claim center location or noisy reconstruction; the exact finite-jet fact is valuable on its own.
residual_risks: Exact high-order Taylor data may be numerically ill-conditioned; no practical error guarantee is supplied.

limitations: r below disjointness and interior margin threshold; convex window, invariant line sampling, equal disk radii only.
No recovery of point labels, positions, congruence, or noisy stability.
